decisions.reason: As a carrier-wafer extension of the firm's core substrate and handling know-how, it remains within high absorptive capacity and can be supported with existing processes, though its narrower niche and weaker visibility make it somewhat more expendable than the firm's current focus areas.

This flagship copper-interposer glass wafer closely matches the firm's direction toward multifunctional packaging wafers, and the firm's in-house R&D and project experience give it the knowledge base to keep learning and improving it commercially.

An off-the-shelf glass and quartz wafer brand is very close to the established business, easy to absorb operationally, and a low-risk way to monetize existing materials and process expertise across several standard models.

Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's core wafer-substrate capabilities, so despite some material overlap the firm is less able to interpret market feedback and improve the product efficiently than in its core lines.
